scope: Replace byte-at-a-time x64, ARM64 and ELF word appends with one existing __buf_reserve call per word; explicitly write little-endian bytes and publish length. This differs from the earlier resize/reserve/setlen/data unaligned-store prototypes.
patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/arm64.jo b/core/compiler/arm64.jo
index eec95bac..59fe0a6f 100644
--- a/core/compiler/arm64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/arm64.jo
@@ -49,11 +49,7 @@ a_stub_fix: (int, int)[]     # BL to a stub
 a_faddr_fix: (int, int)[]    # ADRP + ADD of a function's address
 a_data_fix: (int, int, int)[]    # ADRP + ADD of rodata (kind 0) or data (kind 1) + offset
 
-w32 = (x: int):
-    code.push(u8(x & 255))
-    code.push(u8((x >> 8) & 255))
-    code.push(u8((x >> 16) & 255))
-    code.push(u8((x >> 24) & 255))
+w32 = (x: int): put32(code, x)
 
 rd32 = (p: int) -> int: int(code[p]) | (int(code[p + 1]) << 8) | (int(code[p + 2]) << 16) | (int(code[p + 3]) << 24)
 wr32 = (p: int, x: int):
diff --git a/core/compiler/elf.jo b/core/compiler/elf.jo
index 4384153c..7185a9be 100644
--- a/core/compiler/elf.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/elf.jo
@@ -4,15 +4,34 @@ use 'util.jo'
 
 const ELF_BASE = 0x400000
 
+# Append each encoded word with one uniqueness/growth operation. The runtime
+# returns the unique object header; fill the new bytes before publishing length.
 put16 = (b: mut u8[], v: int):
-    b.push(u8(v & 255))
-    b.push(u8((v >> 8) & 255))
+    old = len(b)
+    p = __buf_reserve(b, 2)
+    p[24 + old + 0] = u8(v & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 1] = u8((v >> 8) & 255)
+    (p as *int)[1] = old + 2
 put32 = (b: mut u8[], v: int):
-    put16(b, v)
-    put16(b, v >> 16)
+    old = len(b)
+    p = __buf_reserve(b, 4)
+    p[24 + old + 0] = u8(v & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 1] = u8((v >> 8) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 2] = u8((v >> 16) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 3] = u8((v >> 24) & 255)
+    (p as *int)[1] = old + 4
 put64 = (b: mut u8[], v: int):
-    put32(b, v)
-    put32(b, v >> 32)
+    old = len(b)
+    p = __buf_reserve(b, 8)
+    p[24 + old + 0] = u8(v & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 1] = u8((v >> 8) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 2] = u8((v >> 16) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 3] = u8((v >> 24) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 4] = u8((v >> 32) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 5] = u8((v >> 40) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 6] = u8((v >> 48) & 255)
+    p[24 + old + 7] = u8((v >> 56) & 255)
+    (p as *int)[1] = old + 8
 
 # the machine (x86-64; arm64: 183) and the page size segments are aligned to (arm64: 64 KB,
 # the largest a Linux kernel there uses)
diff --git a/core/compiler/x64.jo b/core/compiler/x64.jo
index ef02a939..78225fae 100644
--- a/core/compiler/x64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/x64.jo
@@ -31,14 +31,8 @@ data_fix: (int, int, int)[]  # (position of rel32, kind 0=rodata 1=data, offset)
 int_arg_regs = [RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9]
 
 b = (x: int): code.push(u8(x & 255))
-b32 = (x: int):
-    b(x)
-    b(x >> 8)
-    b(x >> 16)
-    b(x >> 24)
-b64 = (x: int):
-    b32(x)
-    b32(x >> 32)
+b32 = (x: int): put32(code, x)
+b64 = (x: int): put64(code, x)
 patch32 = (pos: int, v: int):
     code[pos] = u8(v & 255)
     code[pos + 1] = u8((v >> 8) & 255)

validation.note: The first quick run found an extraction fixture missing the newly shared put32/put64 helpers. The corrected fixture passed using the same C-bootstrapped binary. No full suite or stage gate was run after the flat pilot.

compilation.sample_order: Alternating for two variants; rotating positions and direction for three or more.
compilation.cpu_time_definition: User + system CPU seconds for the compiler and its waited-for children; may exceed wall time with multiple emission workers.

decision: No useful matched compilation gain: default 0.99954, release 1.01049, self-build 1.01568 (self-build inconclusive). Revert rather than pursue another unmeasured emitter micro-optimization. Retain the extra ELF 16/32/64-bit buffer tests.
